headline: A Maryland school board has voted 6 to 1 to ban students from using AI at every grade level, from pre-K through high school.
score_reason: Lowered by one: the vote was on the evening of 7 Oct 2026, before the window.
importance_line: Thousands of students in Frederick County lose AI access in class, but the ban has exceptions, and the district has not yet said how it will enforce them.
summary: FOX 5 DC reports that the Frederick County school board in Maryland voted 6 to 1 on Wednesday night to ban student use of AI from pre-K through 12th grade, citing cheating and over-reliance on technology. The decision reverses course weeks after the district began piloting Google's Gemini for older students, and allows exceptions for lessons about AI and for students with disabilities.
notes: Baltimore Sun original had no readable text; FOX 5 DC covered the same vote and its page is the url.
